# A ternary handed to an option parameter, one arm bare and the other the
# narrowed option, is the option.
#
# Checked expecting the option, the narrowed arm read as the option while the
# ternary took the bare arm's type, so the arms disagreed: Go declared the
# ternary's temp a float64 and assigned it `snglSome(2.0)`, which does not
# compile, and Kotlin and JavaScript were handed a node typed one way holding
# the other.

mkdir none bubbletea android html

cp app.sngl none/app.sngl
sngl test --platform=none none/app.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'

cp app.sngl bubbletea/app.sngl
sngl test --platform=bubbletea bubbletea/app.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'

cp app.sngl android/app.sngl
sngl test --platform=android android/app.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'

cp app.sngl html/app.sngl
sngl test --platform=html html/app.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

var held option[float] = 2.0

func share(flex option[float]) => flex == null ? 0.0 : flex

func shareOr(flex option[float]) => share(flex == null ? 1.0 : flex)

func shareOrInt(flex option[float]) => share(flex != null ? flex : 1)

func testNarrowedArm(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(shareOr(held) == 2.0)
    t.assert(shareOr(null) == 1.0)
}

func testUntypedArm(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(shareOrInt(held) == 2.0)
    t.assert(shareOrInt(null) == 1.0)
}

ui.window {
    ui.text(value="{shareOr(held)}")
}
